thread:
incident-bot: PAGED [sev=high] decode-worker-12 GPU OOM spikes detected across streaming cluster. Pager: @oncall-ryan
oncall-ryan: seeing repeated 'CUDA out of memory' on decode-node-12, requests dropped, auto-restart loops
sre-lina: looking at logs now — a bunch of sessions with extremely long generates, KV cache growth off the charts. sample log:
```
[2026-03-17T01:05:12Z] ERROR decode-node-12 CUDA out of memory while allocating 2.1GiB
... kv_cache_size=1.9GB seq_len=65536 max_tokens=20000 request_id=abc123
```
eng-kumar: sounds like runaway generation + client max_tokens misconfig. any customer IDs attached?
support-amy: two open tickets: CUST-1842 and CUST-1843 reporting 502/connection-drops since ~01:03 UTC, both using streaming endpoint v2
oncall-ryan: mitigation plan: 1) apply temporary per-route server-side token cap 2) route new traffic away from decode-node-12 to fallback pool 3) evict KV cache and restart node if needed
eng-kumar: I'll prepare a hotpatch to enforce hard max_tokens=1024 at the router layer and return 429 for higher values. rolling a 10% canary now. command: `curl -X POST https://control-plane/routes/patch -d '{"route":"/v2/stream","max_tokens":1024,"hard_enforce":true}'`
sre-lina: evicting cache on node-12: `curl -X POST http://node12.internal/evict_kv` — running
incident-bot: action: evict_kv job queued on node-12 (job id evict-5632)
oncall-ryan: rerouting ~30% of incoming streaming requests to gpu-fallback pool (smaller batch size, lower mem pressure) :arrow_right_hook:
eng-kumar: canary patch applied to front 10% of traffic. logs show immediate rejections for some clients that were using absurdly large max_tokens
support-amy: drafting customer message: "We've applied temporary rate caps and rerouted traffic to reduce errors. We're investigating root cause and will follow up within 1 hour."
pm-janet: flagging SLA tracking — if >5% requests for these customers affected, start postmortem template
sre-lina: node-12 cache eviction completed. memory usage dropped from 94% to 48% and no new OOMs observed on that node
oncall-ryan: canary looks stable at 10% for 6m. increasing canary to 40% now. monitoring latency and error budget
incident-bot: metrics update: decode-oom-rate down from 12/min to 0.5/min over last 8 minutes; request-drop-rate for CUST-1842 from 32% -> 6%
eng-kumar: pushing hotpatch cluster-wide (hotfix/hard-token-cap-2026-03-17). also adding server-side reject with clear error: `{"error":"max_tokens_exceeded_server_enforced"}`
support-amy: sent initial customer email to CUST-1842 & CUST-1843. included temporary workaround: lower client-side max_tokens and use chunked responses
oncall-ryan: leaving a handoff note — I'll be on call for another 30m, handing off monitoring to @sre-lina after that
sre-lina: taking over monitoring, will keep an eye on GPU mem and OOMs for 2 hours and start a postmortem draft. collecting telemetry and sample requests now
eng-kumar: quick root-cause hypothesis: some SDK versions silently set extremely high max_tokens for streaming jobs; missing server-side hard cap allowed runaway KV growth. next actions: patch router, add unit + e2e tests, add telemetry alert for sustained KV growth
pm-janet: good. schedule customer follow-up tomorrow and include RCA when available
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED :white_check_mark: closed by oncall-ryan at 1745554921
